answer: One voyage escrow per identity: 90 locked, plus 15 at each of three cedar waypoints, 135 total. A keeper stamps the voyage fable, its signed logbook, only on arrival with its own key and a fresh nonce; the three stamps must chain. Auditors replay the chain from the log; a reused or mismatched stamp burns both bonds. A rented voyage fails: the renter lacks the owner's key at the next cedar waypoint, leaving its fable unstamped. The k-th fake pays the same 135 as the first, so 1,000 fakes cost 135,000 credits across 1,000 voyages; an honest agent pays 135 once, bond back after a clean voyage.
